1000144.etyen:
Internationalism, based on Romanian Moldova. The name originally denoted a river in present-day Romania and was later transferred to the surrounding region and the medieval principality, from which the modern country takes its name.
The deeper origin of the river name is disputed. One modern proposal derives the earliest recorded form, Moldua, from an unattested Old Germanic form *moldwa, interpreted as referring to loose soil along the riverbanks. Celtic, Iranian, Slavic and other old Germanic explanations have also been proposed.
Parallel international adaptations include Danish Moldova, Est

1000912.etyen:
From stor (“great”) + Britannia (“Britain”), literally “Great Britain”, after Latin Britannia Maior (“Great Britain”). The name distinguished the island from Britannia Minor (“Lesser Britain”), namely Bretagne (“Brittany”).
The second element is from Latin Britannia (“Britain”). The Latin name, attested from the first century BCE, derives directly or through Ancient Greek Βρεττανία (Brettanía, “Britain”) and Πρεττανία (Prettanía, “Britain”). The Greek forms ultimately reflect a Celtic ethnonym conventionally reconstructed as early Proto-Brythonic *Pritanī, perhaps from Proto-Celtic *Kʷritanī o
